title: Nanopulse residuals brief — exploratory runs
content:
Purpose: quick write-up of a small set of runs that surfaced recurring ~2–8ms residual latency pulses during sustained low-qps traffic. Trying to capture what I observed, how I reproduced it, and next hypotheses to triage.

Background/context:
- Observed in customer sim where typical qps=3–8 and sequences ~40 tokens. Warm cache expected. Platform: Dedicated pool (A100s), runtime v2.7.1-canary.
- Issue: occasional narrow latency spikes ("nanopulses") that add 2–8ms on top of p50 baseline for a small fraction of requests (~0.4–1.2% depending on run). Not regular cold start or large-scale microburst.

Experiment surface (local cluster repro):
- Script: scripts/loadtests/nanopulse_repro.py (see linked PR for runner config)
- Model: vicuna-13b-8bit-fp16-hybrid (quant profile: q2_8hb)
- Hardware: 1x A100 80GB (no node sharing), CUDA 12.2, cuBLAS/cuDNN stack default
- Workload patterns:
  * steady-1: constant Poisson arrivals, mean qps=5, 95% seq len=40, batch_timeout=6ms, max_batch=16
  * steady-2: same qps but batch_timeout=3ms (attempt tight latency SLO)
  * pulsed: base qps=2 with a 1s spike to qps=30 every 30s
- Duration: 30 minutes per run, 3 warmup minutes discarded

Observed numbers (representative runs, trimmed):
- steady-1 (bt=6ms, warm): p50=10.8ms, p95=28.7ms, p99=94.2ms, nanopulse fraction ~0.9%
- steady-2 (bt=3ms): p50=10.3ms, p95=31.9ms, p99=120.6ms, nanopulse fraction ~1.4%
- pulsed (spike every 30s): p50=11.5ms, p95=34.2ms, p99=128.9ms, nanopulse fraction ~0.6% (mostly outside spikes)

Nanopulse signature (qualitative):
- Very short (2–8ms additional tail) and narrow in time (isolated requests)
- Often correlates with: tiny bumps in device PCIe utilization (~0.5–1% change), short-lived kernel scheduling jitter on the host (2–4ms), and a small KV cache miss burst (12–30 keys missed in 10ms window)
- Happens even after warmups and when batch sizes are near-optimal -> suggests not simple cold-path.

Quick ascii visualization (p99 timeline excerpt, 1-min slice; each char = ~500ms bucket):
[normal]  |====|====|=====|====|==|====|
[nanop]   |===|====|*|====|====|*|====|  ("*" = bucket with >2% nanopulse events)

Low-level traces (sample of one event):
- request id: r-44f9
- timeline (ms): enqueue 0 -> pick/batch 1.2 -> copy-to-device start 1.7 -> kernel-launch 2.3 -> kernel-blocking-preempt 4.8 -> kernel-resume 6.9 -> finish 11.4
- delta compared to clean req: kernel-blocking-preempt stage added ~2.6–4.5ms

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Short-lived kernel preemption/OS scheduling causing tiny stalls during kernel execution. Evidence: host scheduling jitter, correlation with minor PCIe blips.
2) KV cache eviction ripple: a sudden small set of misses causes extra host<->device copies (observed small increase in memcpy counts).
3) Runtime GC/epoch sync in the batching layer causing sub-ms pauses that accumulate under certain alignments with kernel phases.
4) GPU power management transient (less likely — no thermal signature).

Repro tips & commands used:
- Repro runner: python3 scripts/loadtests/nanopulse_repro.py --pattern steady-1 --duration 1800 --seed 821
- To capture deeper traces: ENABLE_TRACING=1 TRACE_DIR=/tmp/trace ./bin/runtime --config conf/test-nanopulse.yaml
- Useful perf counters: ncu for kernel timelines; perf sched for host scheduling; custom KV logging (see linked PR)

Immediate mitigations tried (notes):
- Increase batch_timeout from 3ms -> 8ms: reduced nanopulse fraction by ~0.6 percentage points, but p95 moved slightly up. Tradeoff.
- Pin runtime threads to isolated cores: reduced host scheduling jitter observably, nanopulse fraction dropped ~0.35 percentage points. Promising.
- Forced KV cache prefetch priming before run: tiny effect, not consistent.

Quick conclusions:
- These nanopulses are real, reproducible in a controlled harness, and appear tied to short host-level scheduling or tiny memcpy spikes that add a few ms inside kernel runtime phases.
- Practical mitigation for customers: recommend pinning critical runtime threads + slightly relaxed batch_timeout for latency-sensitive tiny-QPS workloads.

Next steps (actionable):
- 1) Add deterministic kernel-level tracing for the exact preempt window (instrument libcudart callbacks) — low-level task for runtime team. Owner: Samira. Target: 2 weeks.
- 2) Try a run with isolated CPU cores + CPU governor set to performance, also disable C-states on hosts (A/B). Owner: me. Target: this week.
- 3) Explore a two-tier priming: keep a tiny persistent "hedge" batch that runs at 1 qps to keep device memcpy patterns steady. Owner: Diego. Target: spike test next week.
- 4) Open a short-lived telemetry job to track nanospikes across prod clusters (sampling, not full traces). Owner: Observability. Ticket: INF-2819.

Notes-to-self / open questions:
- Could kernel scheduling jitter be introduced by kubelet/node exporter sidecars? Need node-level process lists around events.
- If this maps to an infrequent host interrupt, maybe a NIC/driver path — check dmesg patterns during repro.

Appendix: raw sample of event histogram (counts per ms delta relative to baseline) — trimmed:
0–1ms: 86%
1–2ms: 11%
2–5ms: 2.4%  <-- nanopulse band
5–10ms: 0.5%
>10ms: 0.1%

If anything useful shows up from Samira's kernel traces I'll paste below. For now this is a short running memo so I can iterate quickly.

-- Alfred
